hib-conjugate-vaccine-1987.summary: In 1987 the first conjugate vaccine against Hib was licensed; a leading cause of childhood meningitis nearly disappeared in rich countries. Hib bacteria then caused about 20,000 American cases of meningitis and other invasive disease a year, nearly all in children under five, and young children’s immune systems responded weakly to its sugar coat alone. Chemically linking that polysaccharide to a carrier protein taught infants’ immune systems to recognize it. Invasive Hib disease in US children fell from 40 to 100 cases per 100,000 to fewer than 1 once vaccination became routine.

sources.title: Hib vaccine (Wikipedia)
'Conjugate vaccines', Clinical and Experimental Immunology (PMC 1905528)
sources.author: Clinical and Experimental Immunology
sources.confirms: The first glycoconjugate vaccine for humans, a Hib conjugate, was licensed in the USA in 1987 and soon added to the infant schedule.

sources.title: 'Hib Vaccines: Their Impact on Haemophilus influenzae Type b Disease', Journal of Infectious Diseases 224, suppl. 4 (2021), S321
sources.author: Journal of Infectious Diseases
sources.confirms: Since 1985 polysaccharide and then protein-conjugated Hib vaccines have been licensed in the United States and worldwide.

hib-conjugate-vaccine-1987.detail: Hib disease also included pneumonia and epiglottitis. The vaccines built on work by John Robbins and Rachel Schneerson at NIH and Porter Anderson and David Smith at Boston Children’s Hospital. Hib’s capsule is made of polyribosyl ribitol phosphate, PRP, and antibodies against it protect; in infants, however, responses to plain PRP were variable and faded within months. PRP-D used diphtheria toxoid as its carrier and was first recommended for children aged 18 to 59 months. Conjugate vaccines recruit T cells, producing stronger responses and immune memory, and Hib vaccines now in use are conjugates; by 2013, 184 countries included Hib in routine vaccination, with similar declines in Western Europe and developing countries.

knowledge-navigator-1987.summary: In 1987 Apple's Knowledge Navigator video imagined a tablet with a talking assistant that booked meetings and read papers. Chief executive John Sculley had described such a device in his book Odyssey that year, and his keynote at Educom, a higher education conference, premiered it. The video shows a university professor opening his book-sized tablet; its bow-tied butler reports his waiting calls, then helps him compile Amazon deforestation data for his lecture. Its date is readable as September 2011; Apple launched Siri in October 2011.

sources.title: Knowledge Navigator (Wikipedia)
Computer History Museum, 'Secrets of Siri: Four Milestones in Intelligent Assistance'
sources.author: Computer History Museum
sources.confirms: The museum records that in 1987 John Sculley had Apple's Advanced Technology Group make the Knowledge Navigator concept video, showing a professor using a wireless tablet with a bow-tied assistant that searched, scheduled and placed video calls, set in 2011.

sources.title: Lux, Alex, 'Yesterday's Tomorrows: The Origins of the Tablet', Computer History Museum blog, 17 December 2014
sources.author: Lux, Alex
sources.confirms: Places the Knowledge Navigator among the tablet concepts that preceded the iPad.

knowledge-navigator-1987.detail: The agent helps its user navigate worlds of knowledge by conversation and gesture; the butler pulls up papers and charts and connects a video call with a colleague. Bud Colligan, director of Apple’s higher education marketing, directed it; Hugh Dubberly and Doris Mitsch of Apple Creative Services wrote it, with technical input from Mike Liebhold, who said he was channelling ideas of Alan Kay and MIT’s Architecture Machine group. It took six weeks and $60,000. Apple followed with further concept videos, and New York Times columnist John Markoff has linked Knowledge Navigator to Siri.

lisp-machine-collapse-1987.summary: In 1987 the market for Lisp machines collapsed as cheap workstations ran AI software; the second AI winter began. Lisp machines, built by Symbolics and LISP Machines Inc., were computers optimized for Lisp, American AI research’s preferred language, and corporations had bought them to run in-house expert systems in boom years. Lucid and Franz LISP provided portable LISP environments for UNIX workstations, leaving buyers no reason to pay for single-language hardware. An industry worth half a billion dollars was replaced within a year.

lisp-machine-collapse-1987.detail: By 1985 corporations were spending more than $1 billion a year on AI. Its collapse came three years after Minsky and Schank’s AI winter warning. By the early 1990s most commercial Lisp companies had failed, Symbolics, LISP Machines Inc. and Lucid among them, and Texas Instruments and Xerox gave up on Lisp machines; some customer companies kept maintaining systems written on Lisp machines, in some cases taking over their support.

montreal-protocol-1987.summary: In September 1987 nations agreed in Montreal to phase out chemicals destroying ozone, two years after scientists reported Antarctica’s ozone hole. It set stepped limits on production and consumption of chlorofluorocarbons, halons and other such chemicals, and entered into force on 1 January 1989. Ratified by 198 parties, it became the first universally ratified treaty in United Nations history, and projections have the ozone layer back at 1980 levels across much of Earth by 2040 and over Antarctica by 2066.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Montreal Protocol
Parson, Edward A., Protecting the Ozone Layer: Science and Strategy (Oxford University Press, 2003), ch. 5 'Negotiations and Strategy, 1980-1987', pp. 110-146
sources.author: Parson, Edward A.

montreal-protocol-1987.detail: British Antarctic Survey scientists reported that hole in 1985. Controlled substances are grouped by type, each with its own phase-out schedule, which later amendments tightened. Its adjustments and amendments were agreed in London in 1990, Copenhagen in 1992, Vienna in 1995, Montreal in 1997, Beijing in 1999, Montreal again in 2007, Kigali in 2016 and Quito in 2018. Kigali added hydrofluorocarbons, potent greenhouse gases that had replaced CFCs. Former UN secretary-general Kofi Annan called it “perhaps the single most successful international agreement to date.”

nz-nuclear-free-zone-act-1987.summary: After David Lange's Labour government refused a visit by USS Buchanan in February 1985 because Washington would neither confirm nor deny nuclear weapons aboard, United States suspended its ANZUS obligations to New Zealand. On 8 June 1987 Parliament passed New Zealand Nuclear Free Zone, Disarmament, and Arms Control Act, prohibiting nuclear weapons and nuclear-powered vessels within territory and territorial waters. Reynolds's 1987 study documents public support shaped by French Pacific testing and Rainbow Warrior bombing; Capie's 2019 chapter analyses how a contested policy became bipartisan consensus. National Party abandoned repeal plans in 1990s and law remains in force.

patarroyo-spf66-malaria-vaccine-1987.summary: In 1987 Manuel Elkin Patarroyo's team at Instituto de Inmunología of Hospital San Juan de Dios in Bogotá reported SPf66, a chemically synthesised polymer of peptides from Plasmodium falciparum blood-stage proteins. A paper in March 1988 described protection in volunteers challenged with live parasites, and Colombian field trials followed; Patarroyo donated its patent to WHO in 1993. Trials in Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela and Tanzania reported about 30 percent efficacy, while trials in Gambia and Thailand found none. A 2006 Cochrane review of ten trials concluded SPf66 had no protective effect in Africa and a modest effect in South America, and development stopped. It remained an influential attempt at a synthetic vaccine made outside wealthy countries.

patarroyo-spf66-malaria-vaccine-1987.detail: Patarroyo trained in Bogotá, Yale and Rockefeller University and tested candidate peptides in Aotus monkeys from Amazonian forests, a practice later challenged by Colombian courts over capture of wild primates. SPf66 drew wide press attention in Latin America and a 1994 Príncipe de Asturias prize. GSK's RTS,S, recommended by WHO in 2021, became a malaria vaccine in routine use.

ramayan-doordarshan-1987.summary: From 25 January 1987 state broadcaster Doordarshan aired Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan each Sunday at 9.30 am for 78 episodes. Streets emptied; viewers garlanded television sets and audiences reached an estimated 80 to 100 million as low cost sets spread after 1982 colour conversion and satellite relays. Hindu epic told through video special effects and studio sets became a shared national event and a commercial success for Doordarshan's advertising. Scholars link its reception to rise of Hindu nationalist politics in late 1980s. A 2020 lockdown rerun again drew record audiences, showing durability of this format.

sematech-1987.summary: In 1987 America's government and 14 chipmakers formed SEMATECH to win back manufacturing from Japan, whose chipmakers had overtaken American ones in the mid-1980s; it began operating in Austin, Texas, in 1988. For five years the Department of Defense, through DARPA, matched members’ dues to fund joint research on materials, processes, equipment and lithography. Its board ended government matching after 1996 and turned international, and after a long decline SUNY Polytechnic absorbed it in 2015.

sematech-1987.detail: Conceived in 1986, SEMATECH was funded by DARPA until 1997 and by member dues thereafter, its members representing about half the worldwide chip market. It moved from Austin to Albany, New York, in 2007 after receiving New York state funding, running lithography and metrology programs at the University at Albany’s NanoTech Complex, with its ISMI unit relocating there in 2011. In late 2015 it transferred its Critical Materials Council to TECHCET.

solow-productivity-paradox-1987.summary: In 1987 Robert Solow remarked that the computer age showed up everywhere but in the productivity statistics. His remark appeared on July 12, 1987, reviewing Stephen S. Cohen and John Zysman’s Manufacturing Matters. American labor productivity growth had fallen from 3.8 percent in 1948 to 1.2 percent in 1987, even as information technology’s share of equipment investment tripled. Economists named this gap the productivity paradox and offered explanations: computers were still a small share of capital, service output is poorly measured, and benefits arrive with a lag, as electricity’s had. Productivity growth did rise after 1995, and his quip returns in debates over AI.

sources.title: Joe Santos: Everywhere but in the data
The Solow Productivity Paradox: What Do Computers Do to ...
The Productivity Puzzle: AI, Technology Adoption and ...
Brynjolfsson, Erik, "The productivity paradox of information technology"
sources.author: Erik Brynjolfsson
sources.confirms: Peer-reviewed review that quotes Solow's 12 July 1987 New York Times Book Review remark and surveys the evidence on the paradox.

solow-productivity-paradox-1987.detail: The slowdown dated from about 1973. Jack Triplett’s 1999 Brookings review lists further explanations: hedonic price indexes may overstate inflation-adjusted computer output, some benefits such as convenience never enter statistics, and some computer projects fail outright. From 1996 to 2007 American labor productivity grew 2.7 percent a year on average. A 2024 Richmond Fed brief finds no clear relationship between technology adoption and productivity growth from 1948 to 2022, with trend growth peaking at 3 percent in 2003 and falling to 1 percent by 2015, and suggests AI’s productivity effects may be small.

tsmc-founded-1987.summary: In 1987 Morris Chang founded TSMC to make chips designed by others, a split that let firms like Apple and Nvidia design without factories. Morris Chang founded TSMC to commercialise semiconductor research developed at ITRI, making it the world’s first dedicated foundry, a contract manufacturer fabricating chips designed by others. In 1985 Li Kwoh-ting of Taiwan’s Executive Yuan had invited Chang to lead ITRI and build its chip industry; money was raised in 1986 and operations began in February 1987. Texas Instruments and Intel turned Chang down; only Philips joined. TSMC now holds about 70 percent of global foundry output and supplies Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom and Qualcomm.

sources.confirms: Chang took over ITRI in 1985, devised the pure-play foundry model, and TSMC opened for business in February 1987 with $220 million in capital, half from the government, with Philips as backer; its first customers were Intel, Motorola and TI.

tsmc-founded-1987.verification_note: Chang's oral history, IEEE Spectrum and Britannica put his arrival at ITRI in 1985, with a business plan presented that year, money raised in 1986 and operations starting in February 1987.
tsmc-founded-1987.detail: Philips put up $58 million for a 27.6 percent stake. Taiwan’s government, through its National Development Fund, provided 48.3 percent of TSMC’s startup capital alongside tax benefits. Another 20 percent came from eight private companies owned by some of Taiwan’s wealthiest families, who were asked directly to invest. Fabless designers such as AMD, ARM, MediaTek and Nvidia became customers, as did integrated manufacturers such as Intel and Texas Instruments outsourcing part of their production. TSMC listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1993 and in 1997 became the first Taiwanese company on the New York Stock Exchange. Chang retired in 2018 after 31 years; Mark Liu became chairman and C. C. Wei chief executive. TSMC was first to market with 7-nanometre and 5-nanometre production and first to commercialise ASML’s extreme ultraviolet lithography in high volume. As of June 30, 2026 it was the world’s largest non-US company by market capitalisation.

cmu-sphinx-1986.summary: In 1988 Kai-Fu Lee's Sphinx at Carnegie Mellon recognised continuous speech from any speaker using hidden Markov models. Earlier recognizers had to be trained on one speaker’s voice or heard words one at a time; Sphinx modelled speech sounds statistically and ranked word sequences by probability, so it could understand connected speech from strangers with a large vocabulary, whose feasibility had been in dispute. Carnegie Mellon released Sphinx 2 as open source in 2000 and Sphinx 3 in 2001.

sources.confirms: The HMM-based Sphinx system, unveiled at Carnegie Mellon, was the first to show speaker-independent, large-vocabulary continuous speech recognition.

cmu-sphinx-1986.detail: Its open source releases include acoustic models, training tools and cmudict, a public domain pronunciation dictionary. Sphinx 2, a performance-oriented recognizer written by Xuedong Huang, was released under a BSD-style license on SourceForge by Kevin Lenzo at LinuxWorld in 2000 and used in dialog systems. Sphinx 3 adopted continuous hidden Markov models for high-accuracy work, and PocketSphinx brought Sphinx to embedded systems such as ARM processors with fixed-point arithmetic.

echelon-surveillance-1988.summary: In 1988 Duncan Campbell revealed ECHELON, a system by which five English-speaking countries intercepted the world's telecommunications. ECHELON is a signals intelligence network run by Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Britain and America, the Five Eyes. It grew from stations GCHQ opened at Morwenstow in Cornwall around 1970 to intercept civilian satellite communications. Campbell presented his findings to the European Parliament in 2000; its 2001 report acknowledged ECHELON and concluded it could intercept telephone calls, fax, e-mail and other data traffic globally.

sources.confirms: The author's archive of the 12 August 1988 New Statesman story that first revealed ECHELON as an extension of the UKUSA signals intelligence agreement.

echelon-surveillance-1988.detail: Those five share intelligence under their UKUSA agreement. America’s NSA built a matching station at Yakima, Washington. Also in 1988, Margaret Newsham, working for Lockheed under NSA contract, told members of Congress that ECHELON had collected senator Strom Thurmond’s telephone calls. Congressional investigators determined that targeting of US political figures was no accident but “was designed into the system from the start.” New Zealand journalist Nicky Hager described it in detail in his 1996 book Secret Power. In the 1990s Campbell and Hager said America was exploiting ECHELON traffic for industrial espionage, citing Enercon’s gearless wind turbine and Lernout & Hauspie’s speech technology. In 2000 former CIA director James Woolsey confirmed that US intelligence used interception and keyword searches to monitor European businesses. The European Parliament’s 2001 resolution admitted that European legislators had little power to change it.

global-polio-eradication-initiative-1988.summary: In 1988 the world resolved to eradicate polio; cases fell from an estimated 350,000 that year to 650 confirmed in 2012, and only two countries remain endemic. WHO, Rotary International, America's CDC and UNICEF then created their Global Polio Eradication Initiative, with Nick Ward as its first coordinator. Polio was then endemic in 125 countries. Its strategy built on methods that had controlled wild poliovirus across the Americas and on smallpox eradication: mass childhood immunisation with oral vaccine, surveillance of acute flaccid paralysis in children under 15, and “mop up” campaigns wherever cases appear.

World Health Assembly, Resolution WHA41.28, 'Global eradication of poliomyelitis by the year 2000', May 1988
sources.author: World Health Assembly
sources.confirms: The May 1988 World Health Assembly resolution committing the world to eradicate poliomyelitis by 2000.

sources.title: World Health Organization, 'Poliomyelitis' (fact sheet)
sources.author: World Health Organization
sources.confirms: In 1988 the World Health Assembly resolved to eradicate polio, launching the Global Polio Eradication Initiative; wild poliovirus cases fell from about 350,000 in more than 125 countries in 1988 to two endemic countries, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

global-polio-eradication-initiative-1988.detail: Rotary International had begun its campaign in 1987, aiming to raise $100 million against polio by its 100th anniversary. Wild poliovirus had been brought under control across the Americas in the early 1980s, and paralysis surveillance finds where virus persists. Since 1995 a Global Certification Commission has certified eradication region by region: Western Pacific and American regions qualified by 2000, India was certified polio-free in 2014 and Africa in 2020. Afghanistan and Pakistan remained the only endemic countries as of 2021. At its peak it employed 4,000 people across 75 countries on nearly $1 billion a year. By 2021 it had raised $18 billion, with Gates Foundation money providing a large portion, and WHO calls it history’s largest international public health initiative.

picture.credit: CDC Global, CC BY 2.0, via CDC Global (mirrored on Wikimedia Commons)

hansen-climate-testimony-1988.summary: In June 1988 James Hansen told the Senate that global warming had begun and was caused by humans; climate change became news. Director of NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies, he said global warming was already happening and greenhouse gases could be linked with observed warming with high confidence. In his words, “Global warming has reached a level such that we can ascribe with a high degree of confidence a cause and effect relationship between the greenhouse effect and observed warming.” NASA, he said, was 99 percent confident that accumulating greenhouse gases, not random fluctuation, caused it. Science historian Spencer Weart credits his testimony with increasing public awareness of climate change.

hansen-climate-testimony-1988.detail: Hansen also told senators that “The greenhouse effect has been detected and it is changing our climate now,” and he led GISS from 1981 to 2013. That year he published his first climate prediction computed from a general circulation model, estimating mean surface temperature under several emissions scenarios. He concluded that warming would be evident within decades and would bring temperatures at least as high as those of the Eemian interglacial. He called a rise of 0.4 °C above the 1950–1980 mean his “smoking gun” for human-caused warming. Richard Besel of California Polytechnic State University called his testimony “an important turning point in the history of global climate change,” and Timothy O’Donnell of the University of Mary Washington judged it a decisive moment.

imparja-television-1988.summary: When Australia's AUSSAT satellite promised to beam commercial television into remote communities in mid-1980s, Aboriginal organisations feared cultural damage and lobbied for ownership. Central Australian Aboriginal Media Association (CAAMA) won Remote Commercial Television Service licence for central zone in 1986 against a commercial rival, and Imparja Television went to air on 15 January 1988 from Alice Springs, reaching Northern Territory, South Australia and parts of neighbouring states. Eric Michaels's study of Warlpiri video at Yuendumu had shown communities making their own television with low-power transmitters from 1985. Imparja carried Aboriginal-produced programmes such as Nganampa Anwernekenhe alongside commercial content, funding news and language programming.

imparja-television-1988.detail: Michaels's Aboriginal Invention of Television, published in 1986, remains a landmark in media anthropology, arguing Warlpiri video had its own aesthetics and rules about images of deceased people. Imparja faced tension between commercial survival and Aboriginal content. National Indigenous Television (NITV) launched in 2007 and joined SBS in 2012. BRACS scheme put community video units in 80 remote settlements from 1987.

inpe-prodes-deforestation-monitoring-198.summary: In 1988 Brazil's Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE), in São José dos Campos, started PRODES, an annual survey of clear-cut deforestation across Brazil's Legal Amazon using Landsat images interpreted by its own analysts, following a pilot assessment for 1978. PRODES published yearly deforestation rates that became official national figures and were taken up in climate negotiations. From 2004 INPE added DETER, a same-day alert system using MODIS and later CBERS imagery that directed IBAMA enforcement raids. Assunção, Gandour and Rocha's 2023 study estimates that DETER-guided enforcement cut deforestation substantially between 2006 and 2011. In 2019 President Bolsonaro dismissed INPE's director Ricardo Galvão after disputing data showing clearing rising again.

inpe-prodes-deforestation-monitoring-198.detail: INPE had received Landsat data at Cuiabá since 1973 and built China-Brazil CBERS satellites from 1999, giving Brazil its own optical imagery. PRODES figures showed deforestation falling from 27,772 square kilometres in 2004 to 4,571 in 2012, then rising after 2015. TerraBrasilis now publishes these data openly, and INPE's methods have been adapted in other tropical countries.

ipcc-founded-1988.summary: In 1988 the UN created the IPCC to assess climate science for governments; its reports set the terms of every climate negotiation. UN endorsement followed later that year. Its purpose is to give governments scientific information they can use to develop climate policies. It conducts no research of its own; instead it assesses published literature on climate change, its impacts, risks and possible responses, with thousands of scientists volunteering to review its drafts. Its First Assessment Report appeared in 1990, and it shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
United Nations General Assembly, Resolution 43/53, 'Protection of Global Climate for Present and Future Generations of Mankind', A/RES/43/53, 6 December 1988
sources.author: United Nations General Assembly
sources.confirms: The resolution of 6 December 1988 endorses the joint establishment of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change by WMO and UNEP to provide coordinated scientific assessments of climate change for governments.

ipcc-founded-1988.detail: IPCC assessments cover climate change’s natural, economic and social impacts and risks. Its 195 member states govern it from its secretariat in Geneva, hosted by WMO; they elect a bureau of scientists for each assessment cycle, usually six to seven years, and that bureau selects experts nominated by governments and observer organizations. Three working groups and one task force carry out its scientific work, and synthesis reports integrate their findings. Each report covers papers published before a set deadline and notes where science has improved since its predecessor. Its Fifth Assessment Report influenced 2015’s Paris Agreement. Working Group I’s contribution to its Sixth, published in August 2021, drew from the Guardian its “starkest warning yet,” and its seventh cycle began in 2023.

iran-regulated-kidney-donation-1988.summary: Facing long dialysis queues and no cadaveric donation law, Iran's Ministry of Health in 1988 authorises a programme in which unrelated living donors give a kidney for a fixed government payment plus a year of health insurance, with a charitable patient association, not brokers, matching pairs and transplant teams barred from payment. Transplant numbers rise from a few hundred a year to about 1,500 by late 1990s, and programme insiders Ghods and Savaj report in 2006 that renal transplant waiting list had been eliminated. No other country runs such a scheme. Ethicists and transplant societies argue over whether it is a model or exploitation of poor donors, and later surveys of donor welfare qualify its early claims.

iran-regulated-kidney-donation-1988.detail: Ghods and Savaj described programme rules and outcomes from inside in 2006; a 2023 review follows its later evolution. Transplantation Society's position paper disputes waiting-list claims and notes donor hardship.

moravecs-paradox-1988.summary: In 1988 Hans Moravec observed that computers find chess easy and walking hard, the reverse of humans, a pattern known as Moravec's paradox: adult-level reasoning comes easily to machines that struggle with a one-year-old’s perception and mobility. He explained it by evolution: skills such as recognizing faces or walking took millions of years to develop and run unconsciously, so they look effortless, while abstract reasoning is evolutionarily recent, and he expected reverse-engineering any skill to be roughly as hard as that skill is old.

raw
Hans Moravec, Mind Children: The Future of Robot and Human Intelligence (Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 1988)
sources.author: Moravec, Hans
sources.confirms: Publisher's record of the 1988 monograph that states the paradox that high-level reasoning needs little computation while sensorimotor skills need enormous resources.

moravecs-paradox-1988.detail: Moravec stated his paradox directly. In Moravec’s words, “it is comparatively easy to make computers exhibit adult level performance on intelligence tests or playing checkers, and difficult or impossible to give them the skills of a one-year-old when it comes to perception and mobility.” He located “a billion years of experience about the nature of the world and how to survive in it” in the brain’s large, highly evolved sensory and motor portions. Abstract thought, he wrote, “is a new trick, perhaps less than 100 thousand years old,” by comparison. By his argument, skills that require conscious effort, such as mathematics, logic and games, need not be difficult to engineer at all. Rodney Brooks, Marvin Minsky and others articulated similar observations in the 1980s.

morris-worm-1988.summary: In November 1988 a student's worm disabled about a tenth of the internet's 60,000 computers; DARPA responded by funding the CERT Coordination Center at Carnegie Mellon. Robert Morris, a Cornell graduate student, wrote it, by his friend’s account, to see if it could be done. It entered machines through holes in Unix sendmail and finger and through weak passwords, and because it reinfected machines already carrying it, repeated copies slowed computers to unusability. It is usually reported to have infected around 6,000 major UNIX machines, and Morris received the first felony conviction under 1986's Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

morris-worm-1988.detail: Morris released his worm from MIT so that it would not be traced to Cornell. It exploited sendmail’s debug mode, a buffer overflow in fingerd and trust between machines via rexec and rsh. Its main body ran on DEC VAX machines running 4BSD and on Sun-3 systems; Michael Rabin, whose ideas on randomization inspired its copying rate, later said Morris “should have tried it on a simulator first.” Clifford Stoll wrote that he found 2,000 infected computers within fifteen hours. Many sites disconnected from the NSFNET backbone and from each other while cleaning their networks. Appeals judges put removal costs at $200 to $53,000 per installation; Stoll estimated total economic impact for the Government Accountability Office at between $100,000 and $10,000,000. Morris was sentenced to three years’ probation, 400 hours of community service and a fine. DARPA responded by funding the CERT Coordination Center at Carnegie Mellon.

ofeq-1-shavit-launch-1988.summary: On 19 September 1988 Israel Aerospace Industries launches Ofeq-1, a 155 kilogram experimental satellite, from Palmachim air base on a three-stage Shavit rocket derived from Jericho missile work. To avoid overflying Arab neighbours, rocket flies west against Earth's rotation, giving up payload for a retrograde orbit, a choice no other launching state had made. Satellite carries no camera but tests power, telemetry and tracking; Ofeq-3 in 1995 begins imaging. Israel becomes eighth state to orbit its own satellite on its own launcher. Analysts read launch as demonstration of missile reach as much as a civil achievement, and it anchors a space industry that later sells imaging satellites and builds Beresheet lunar lander.

polymer-banknote-australia-1988.summary: After a 1966 wave of forged ten-dollar notes, Reserve Bank of Australia asked CSIRO chemists, led by David Solomon, to design a note that could not be copied. Team developed a biaxially oriented polypropylene substrate coated with opaque layers, leaving a clear window carrying an optically variable device, a diffraction grating image of Captain Cook. On 26 January 1988 bank issued a commemorative ten-dollar polymer note for Australia's bicentenary. Early notes suffered ink wear, and full series followed from 1992 to 1996, making Australia first country with all-polymer currency. Note Printing Australia and Securency licensed technology to more than 30 countries, including Canada, Britain and Mexico.

Polymer notes last several times longer than paper, resist water and are recycled. Solomon's polymer chemistry group also discovered nitroxide-mediated living radical polymerisation, described in his 2005 review. A 2011 bribery scandal involving Securency executives selling technology abroad led to prosecutions. Reserve Bank's 1988 annual report records bicentennial issue.

saudi-aramco-created-1988.summary: In 1988 Saudi Arabia, full owner of Aramco since 1980, reorganised it as Saudi Aramco, now the most valuable oil company on Earth. Aramco, the Arabian American Oil Company, had been formed by American oil majors and kept operating Saudi fields on Saudi Arabia’s behalf until 1988, when a November royal decree created Saudi Arabian Oil Company to take control of its assets.

saudi-aramco-created-1988.detail: Standard Oil of California found oil at Dammam in 1938. Its company was renamed from California-Arabian Standard Oil Co. to Arabian American Oil Co. on 31 January 1944. On 17 March 1947 Standard Oil of New Jersey, later Exxon, bought 30 percent and Socony Vacuum, later Mobil, 10 percent, with SoCal and Texaco keeping 30 percent each. In 1989 and 1990 high-quality oil and gas were discovered in three areas south of Riyadh, and in 1990 Saudi Aramco began expanding crude sales into Asia.

tat-8-fiber-optic-cable-1988.summary: In 1988 TAT-8, the first fibre-optic cable across the Atlantic, carried 40,000 calls at once, ten times its copper predecessor. Its 280 megabits per second carried 40,000 telephone circuits, far beyond earlier copper cables. AT&T Bell Laboratories developed its technology. Opto-electric-opto regenerators spaced along the seabed convert light pulses back to electrical signals and resend them, at lower cost and wider spacing than earlier cables’ electrical repeaters. Its capacity filled within eighteen months, and it carried early transatlantic internet traffic.

tat-8-fiber-optic-cable-1988.detail: Glass fibers carry its light pulses. An innovative branching unit on the continental shelf off Great Britain let one crossing serve three countries. Landings are at Tuckerton, New Jersey, Widemouth Bay, England, and Penmarch, France. Forecasters had predicted its capacity would not fill for a decade, and some that it would never fill and no further cables would be needed. In 1989, with this new capacity, IBM agreed to fund a dedicated T1 link between Cornell University and CERN, completed in February 1990. It greatly increased connectivity between American and European portions of the early Internet. Early reliability problems in its first two years stemmed mainly from manufacturing defects; a 1985 trial cable off the Canary Islands, lacking an electrical screen, had been attacked by sharks drawn to its high-voltage lines. TAT-8 was retired in 2002.

td-learning-sutton-1988.summary: In 1988 Sutton formalised temporal-difference learning, predicting from the difference between successive guesses; it later trained AlphaGo. Conventional prediction learning assigns credit by the difference between predicted and actual outcomes, waiting for Saturday to correct a week of weather forecasts. TD methods instead correct each prediction from the next, so Friday’s forecast adjusts Monday’s before Saturday arrives. Sutton proved their convergence and optimality for special cases and argued they need less memory and computation. His approach built on Arthur Samuel’s checkers work and powered Gerald Tesauro’s TD-Gammon.

sources.title: Sutton (1988), Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences, Machine Learning
Temporal difference learning (Wikipedia)
Sutton, Richard S., 'Learning to predict by the methods of temporal differences', Machine Learning (1988)
sources.author: Sutton, Richard S.
sources.confirms: The abstract says conventional methods assign credit using the difference between predicted and actual outcomes, while temporal-difference methods use the difference between temporally successive predictions.

td-learning-sutton-1988.detail: Such methods, Sutton’s abstract notes, had been used in Samuel’s checker player, John Holland’s bucket brigade and his own Adaptive Heuristic Critic but had “remained poorly understood” until then. He argued that they predict more accurately and that most problems then handled by supervised learning are prediction problems suited to TD methods. He showed that TD(1) can, under many circumstances, need only a fraction 1/M of the memory and speed of the conventional Widrow–Hoff procedure, where M is the longest sequence. His TD-Lambda algorithm let Tesauro’s TD-Gammon learn backgammon at expert human level, and neuroscientists later found that dopamine neurons’ firing rates appear to mimic its error signal.

thailand-shrimp-farming-boom-1988.summary: Hatchery techniques for Penaeus monodon, aerated high-density ponds and Japanese demand drive a rush into intensive shrimp farming along Thailand's upper Gulf coast from around 1987. Farmed output rises from about 34,000 tonnes in 1987 to 122,000 tonnes in 1991, when Thailand overtakes Taiwan and China as leading exporter of farmed shrimp. Mangrove clearance, saline intrusion into rice fields and disease outbreaks force farmers to abandon ponds within a few years and move down coast, a roving pattern of resource use. Vietnam, Indonesia and India later follow Thai methods.

ubiquitous-computing-1988.summary: In 1988 Mark Weiser at Xerox PARC coined ubiquitous computing, computers everywhere and invisible; the phone in your pocket is his forecast. He envisioned computing made to appear anytime and everywhere, rather than confined to a desktop. Alone and with PARC director John Seely Brown, he wrote the earliest papers defining his field. He proposed three device forms: tabs, wearable and inch-sized; pads, hand-held and foot-sized; and boards, interactive displays about a meter across. PARC built them as PARCTab, PARCPad and LiveBoard, early prototypes of handheld, tablet and large-display computing.

sources.title: Ubiquitous computing (Wikipedia)
Weiser, Mark, 'The Computer for the 21st Century', Scientific American (1991)
sources.author: Weiser, Mark
sources.confirms: The page says specialized hardware and software connected by wires, radio waves, and infrared will be ubiquitous and go unnoticed.
sources.qualifies: The article presents ubiquitous computing as a forecast in 1991, rather than documenting the 1988 coinage.

sources.title: Weiser, Mark, 'The Computer for the 21st Century', Pervasive Computing (2002)
sources.author: Weiser, Mark
sources.confirms: The page says Weiser coined the term in 1988 for a future of invisible computers embedded in everyday objects, and describes computing that vanishes into the background; it names tabs, pads, and boards as device forms.
sources.qualifies: It dates Weiser’s coinage to 1988, but describes tabs as inch-scale and pads as foot-scale, rather than about a centimeter and a decimeter.

ubiquitous-computing-1988.verification_note: A 2002 source dates the coining to 1988 and gives tabs as inch-scale and pads as foot-scale rather than centimetre and decimetre; Weiser's 1991 article presents ubiquitous computing as a forecast.
ubiquitous-computing-1988.detail: Ubiquitous computing can occur on any device, in any location and format, and can involve everyday objects such as a refrigerator or a pair of glasses. Weiser drew on philosophy, phenomenology, anthropology, psychology, post-modernism, sociology of science and feminist criticism, and cited Philip K. Dick’s novel Ubik. Natalie Jeremijenko’s “Live Wire,” or Dangling String, installed at PARC during his tenure, was string on a stepper motor that twitched with network traffic. Weiser called it an example of calm technology. His concept is also described as pervasive computing, ambient intelligence or “everyware,” and, when objects are in focus, as physical computing.

aarnet-internet-australia-1989.summary: Australian Academic and Research Network, formed by Australian Vice-Chancellors' Committee and CSIRO, opened a 56-kilobit satellite link between University of Melbourne and University of Hawai'i on 23 June 1989, connecting Australia to NSFNET and wider Internet with TCP/IP. Earlier ACSnet had carried store-and-forward email since 1970s via dial-up to United States. Robert Elz and Geoff Huston led technical work; Huston became AARNet's first technical manager. Universities and research agencies joined within months. By mid-1990s AARNet also served commercial customers, and in 1995 it sold that customer base to Telstra, seeding Australia's commercial ISP industry. NASA's Pacific Communications link made Hawai'i the gateway.

Clarke's chapter for Virtual Nation details ACSnet, early .au domain administration by Elz and 1989 switch to IP. AARNet now runs high-capacity national fibre and connects to Pacific and Asia. New Zealand's first Internet link, from University of Waikato to Hawai'i via PACCOM, opened in April 1989, a few weeks earlier, so Australasia's connection came through Hawai'i in both cases.

aral-sea-divides-1989.summary: Fourth largest lake on earth in 1960 at 68,000 square kilometres, Aral Sea receives almost no inflow after Soviet canals, Karakum among them, take Amu Darya and Syr Darya water for cotton and rice across Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan. Level drops 14 metres by 1989, when a shrinking body separates into a Small Aral in north and a Large Aral in south. Fishing fleets at Muynak and Aralsk lie stranded kilometres from water, 24 native fish species vanish, and dust storms carry salt and pesticide residue from exposed seabed across Karakalpakstan, where respiratory and kidney disease rise. Kazakhstan's Kok-Aral dike, finished in 2005 with World Bank funding, revives Small Aral; eastern Large Aral dries completely in 2014.

basel-convention-1989.summary: In March 1989 the Basel Convention restricted shipping hazardous waste to poor countries. It entered into force on 5 May 1992. Tighter environmental laws had raised rich countries’ disposal costs, and toxic waste dumped in Haiti and Nigeria prompted calls for regulation. It governs cross border shipments of hazardous waste, including discarded electronics, through prior informed consent of receiving states; amendments agreed in May 2019 extended it to plastic waste, binding on 186 states. The United States signed but never ratified.

sources.title: Basel Convention (Wikipedia)
Secretariat of the Basel Convention, "History of the negotiations of the Basel Convention"
sources.author: Secretariat of the Basel Convention (UNEP)
sources.confirms: Adopted 22 March 1989, in force 5 May 1992, to control transboundary movements of hazardous waste, especially to developing countries.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection, Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, chapter XXVII.3
sources.author: United Nations
sources.confirms: Depositary record of the treaty and its parties.

basel-convention-1989.detail: Disposal costs rose in the 1970s as laws tightened, while cheaper shipping and poorer countries’ need for foreign currency opened outlets for waste. In 1986 to 1988 the ship Khian Sea unloaded Philadelphia incinerator ash on a Haitian beach, and in 1988 five ships carried 8,000 barrels of hazardous waste from Italy to Koko, Nigeria, in exchange for $100 a month paid to one farmer for use of his land. The convention bans waste trade between parties and non-parties unless another treaty covers it; America, a non-party, relies on such agreements. Its original text prohibited exports only to Antarctica, and developing countries, Greenpeace and several European states argued at its 1995 conference for a full ban. The resulting Ban Amendment prohibits hazardous waste exports from developed to developing countries for any reason, recycling included. It entered into force on 5 December 2019 after Croatia became its 97th ratifier.

bougainville-panguna-mine-closure-1989.summary: Panguna, opened in 1972 by Bougainville Copper Limited (majority owned by Conzinc Riotinto of Australia), was among world's largest open-cut copper and gold mines and produced about 45 percent of Papua New Guinea's exports. It dumped tailings into Kawerong and Jaba rivers and paid small royalties to landowners. In 1988 Francis Ona and Pepetua Serero's Panguna Landowners Association demanded 10 billion kina compensation; sabotage of power pylons began that November. Mine suspended operations on 15 May 1989 and never reopened. Conflict between Bougainville Revolutionary Army and PNG forces, with a blockade from 1990, killed up to 15,000 people before a 1998 ceasefire and 2001 peace agreement.

bougainville-panguna-mine-closure-1989.detail: Regan's 1998 analysis distinguishes landowner grievances, secessionist history dating to 1975 and generational tension within Nasioi communities. Allen's 2018 chapter places Panguna among resource conflicts in Melanesia. Denoon's Getting Under the Skin, reviewed by Banks, examines 1967 Bougainville Copper Agreement negotiated by Australian administration. A 2019 referendum saw 97.7 percent vote for independence; mine site remains closed, with legacy pollution and periodic proposals to reopen it under Bougainville control.

cold-fusion-claim-1989.summary: In March 1989 two Utah chemists announced fusion in a jar at room temperature; nobody could repeat it, and the episode became a byword. Their tabletop apparatus passed electric current through heavy water on a palladium electrode. It produced, they reported, anomalous “excess heat” of a magnitude that would defy explanation except in terms of nuclear processes, along with small amounts of neutrons and tritium. Many scientists tried to replicate it, but numerous attempts failed and some positive results were later retracted or challenged; by late 1989 most scientists considered the claims dead.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cold fusion
Fleischmann, Martin and Pons, Stanley, 'Electrochemically Induced Nuclear Fusion of Deuterium', Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry 261 (1989) 301-308
sources.author: Fleischmann, Martin; Pons, Stanley
sources.confirms: The original claim published after the 23 March 1989 press conference.

sources.title: 'Cold fusion', Encyclopaedia Britannica
sources.author: Encyclopaedia Britannica
sources.confirms: In 1989 Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons announced they had produced fusion at essentially room temperature.
sources.qualifies: Britannica does not give the March date or discuss the failed replications.

cold-fusion-claim-1989.detail: Neutrons and tritium are byproducts of deuterium fusion. Their announcement drew wide media attention and raised hopes of cheap, abundant energy. Utah’s administration, wanting priority over Steven Jones’s team at Brigham Young University, pressed Fleischmann and Pons to disclose their work before both groups’ planned joint submission to Nature. Their press release claimed Nature would publish their paper, which went instead to the Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry. In 1989 America’s Department of Energy concluded that reported excess heat did not present convincing evidence of a useful energy source and declined to fund cold fusion specifically; its second review in 2004 reached similar conclusions. Cold fusion gained a reputation as pathological science, and articles on it rarely appear in mainstream peer-reviewed journals.

deep-thought-chess-1989.summary: In 1989 Garry Kasparov beat Deep Thought easily in both games of a match; its builders went on to make Deep Blue. Designed at Carnegie Mellon University and later developed at IBM, it was second in Feng-hsiung Hsu’s line of chess computers, after ChipTest and before Deep Blue. In 1988 it had become the first computer to beat a grandmaster in a regular tournament game, defeating Bent Larsen, and in 1989 it won the World Computer Chess Championship.

sources.confirms: On 22 October 1989 at the New York Academy of Art Kasparov won both games of a two-game match against Deep Thought.

deep-thought-chess-1989.detail: Deep Thought won 1988’s North American Computer Chess Championship and held US Chess Federation rating 2551. Besides Hsu, its team included Thomas Anantharaman, Mike Browne, Murray Campbell and Andreas Nowatzyk. It also lost by correspondence against Michael Valvo. Its name came from Douglas Adams’s fictional computer in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, naming continued by Deep Blue, Deep Fritz and Deep Junior.

exxon-valdez-1989.summary: In March 1989 tanker Exxon Valdez spilled 11 million gallons of crude into Prince William Sound; Congress required double hulls on tankers. It was carrying 53.1 million gallons when it hit the reef at 12:04 a.m. after steering out of its shipping lane to avoid icebergs, and eight of eleven cargo holds were punctured. Oil eventually reached 1,300 miles of coastline, 200 of them heavily oiled, in habitat for salmon, sea otters, seals and seabirds, and Congress responded with the Oil Pollution Act of 1990.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Exxon Valdez oil spill
'Prologue', in Oil in the Environment: Legacies and Lessons of the Exxon Valdez Oil Spill (Cambridge University Press)
sources.author: Cambridge University Press
sources.confirms: Shortly after midnight on 24 March 1989 the Exxon Valdez grounded on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound, rupturing eight of eleven tanks and releasing some 11 million gallons of crude.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Exxon Valdez oil spill'
sources.author: Encyclopaedia Britannica
sources.confirms: The spill of 24 March 1989 in Prince William Sound after the tanker ran aground on Bligh Reef.

exxon-valdez-1989.detail: Exxon Shipping Company owned the tanker, bound for Long Beach, California; Bligh Reef lies six miles west of Tatitlek. Captain Joseph Hazelwood had left third mate Gregory Cousins in charge of his bridge; the oil came from Alaska’s Prudhoe Bay field. About 10.8 million gallons escaped, 5.8 million of them within three hours and fifteen minutes. Prince William Sound’s remote location, reachable only by helicopter, plane or boat, made response difficult. A 1989 Coast Guard report found that neither Exxon, Alyeska Pipeline Service Company, Alaska nor federal agencies had been prepared for such a spill. It remains America’s second largest spill after Deepwater Horizon in 2010 and its costliest disaster with no direct human fatalities. Jurors awarded $5 billion in punitive damages in 1994; after Exxon’s appeals reached the Supreme Court in 2008, that award was cut to $507.5 million. Exxon spent an estimated $2 billion on cleanup and $1 billion settling civil and criminal charges.

game-boy-1989.summary: In April 1989 Nintendo released the Game Boy, a grey handheld with a green screen; bundled with Tetris, it sold an estimated 118.69 million units with the Game Boy Color. Nintendo Research & Development 1, under Gunpei Yokoi and Satoru Okada, designed it to expand on Game & Watch with a dot-matrix display and interchangeable cartridges. They prioritized affordability, battery life and durability over rivals’ color graphics and processing power, with its monochrome screen, 8-bit processor and four AA batteries.

National Museum of American History, 'Game Boy', object nmah_1253117
sources.author: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
sources.confirms: The catalogue records the 1989 release, the monochrome LCD, the Tetris bundle on all original units, and over 100 million Game Boy and Game Boy Color units shipped.

sources.author: New York Times
sources.confirms: The obituary names Yokoi as the Game Boy's chief designer, launched in 1989, with about 55 million sold by 1997.

sources.confirms: Catalogue entry for the 1989 Japanese-made DMG-01 console.

game-boy-1989.detail: Rival handhelds came from Sega, Atari and NEC. Its initial Japanese shipment of 300,000 sold out in two weeks. Yokoi called his approach “lateral thinking with withered technology,” using mature, low-cost components. Henk Rogers, who held rights to Tetris, convinced Nintendo of America president Minoru Arakawa to bundle it instead of Super Mario Land, arguing that Tetris would appeal to everyone. Tetris shipped with Game Boy in every region except Japan and went on to sell more than 35 million copies. Its US launch at $89.95, backed by a $20 million marketing campaign, sold 40,000 units on its first day and a million within weeks; by 1995 Nintendo of America reported that 46 percent of Game Boy players were female. Pokémon Red, Blue and Yellow sold more than 46 million copies and kept the system popular late into the 1990s, and Game Boy entered the National Toy Hall of Fame in 2009.

gnu-gpl-1989.summary: In 1989 Stallman released the GNU General Public License, which lets anyone share code on condition they share changes; Linux adopted it. Stallman wrote it for his GNU Project to unify similar licenses he had attached to GNU Emacs, GDB and GCC, each specific to its program. Copyleft works through copyright law: whoever distributes copies or modified versions must make human-readable source available under identical terms. Version 2 followed in 1991 and version 3 in 2007; Linux’s kernel and GCC use it.

sources.title: GNU General Public License (Wikipedia)
Free Software Foundation, 'GNU General Public License, Version 1', February 1989
sources.author: Free Software Foundation; Stallman, Richard M.
sources.confirms: The license text dated February 1989 requires that any distributed work containing the program, with or without modifications, be licensed to all third parties under the same terms.

sources.title: Kelty, Christopher M. Two Bits: The Cultural Significance of Free Software. Durham, NC: Duke University Press, 2008. Chapter 6, 'Writing Copyright Licenses', pp. 179-209.
sources.author: Christopher M. Kelty
sources.confirms: University-press chapter tracing how Stallman consolidated the Emacs and GCC licenses into the GNU General Public License released in 1989; Crossref metadata confirmed.

gnu-gpl-1989.detail: Stallman founded the Free Software Foundation, which publishes it; his program-specific licenses had been incompatible with each other, and copyleft passes freedoms down chains of recipients. GPLv1 targeted two ways distributors restricted software: publishing only executable binaries, and adding restrictions directly or by combining programs under different terms. Copyleft applies only on redistribution; private modified versions carry no obligation to publish changes, and programs merely running on a GPL-licensed operating system need not be GPL-licensed. GPLv2 appeared in June 1991 alongside the Library General Public License, and GPLv3 in June 2007 after concerns about tivoization and patent deals. David A. Wheeler argues that copyleft made Linux-based systems’ success possible by assuring contributors that their work would remain free. In 2011, according to Black Duck Software, 42.5 percent of open-source projects used GPLv2 and 6.5 percent GPLv3; Linus Torvalds kept Linux’s kernel on version 2.

iran-family-planning-programme-1989.summary: In December 1989 Iran's government, with clerical endorsement, reverses a decade of pronatalist policy and makes contraception free through health houses, rural clinics and urban centres staffed by behvarz community workers. Pills, condoms, IUDs and sterilisation are offered, premarital counselling becomes compulsory, and 1993 legislation removes benefits for fourth children. Total fertility falls from about 6.8 births per woman in mid-1980s to replacement level around 2000, among steepest declines recorded anywhere, with rural fertility converging on urban. Demographers credit health infrastructure built after 1985, rising female schooling and religious legitimation rather than coercion. Policy is reversed again after 2012 when leadership calls for population growth and restricts services.

lenet-1989.summary: In 1989 LeCun's convolutional network read handwritten ZIP codes at Bell Labs; the design now reads every image a computer sees. A zip code network published at Bell Labs in November 1988 still had hand-tuned early layers, and Wei Zhang's group in Japan had trained a two-dimensional convolutional network by backpropagation for character recognition in 1988. LeCun’s network learned its convolutional kernels, small filters slid across each image to detect strokes wherever they occur, from data by backpropagation. It was later called LeNet-1 and tested on U.S. Postal Service ZIP code data, with reported error of 1% and rejections of about 9%. Its descendants read bank cheques by the millions.

sources.title: LeNet
LeCun, Y., Boser, B., Denker, J. S., Henderson, D., Howard, R. E., Hubbard, W. and Jackel, L. D., 'Backpropagation Applied to Handwritten Zip Code Recognition', Neural Computation 1 (1989) 541-551
sources.author: LeCun, Yann; Boser, Bernhard; Denker, John S.; Henderson, Donnie; Howard, Richard E.; Hubbard, Wayne; Jackel, Lawrence D.

lenet-1989.verification_note: Schmidhuber's annotated history notes Wei Zhang and colleagues in Japan trained a two-dimensional CNN by backpropagation for character recognition in 1988, making LeCun's 1989 paper the second journal submission on backpropagation-trained CNNs.
lenet-1989.detail: LeCun had joined Bell Labs’ Adaptive Systems Research Department in Holmdel, New Jersey, under Lawrence D. Jackel in October 1988; Denker's group built its November 1988 network. Its data were 9,298 grayscale images of 16×16 pixels digitized from zip codes on mail passing through Buffalo, New York’s post office, 7,291 for training and 2,007 for testing, ambiguous and misclassified examples included. Two humans made errors at 2.5 percent on average on its test set. Training took three days on a Sun-4/260 over 23 epochs. LeCun’s series ran to LeNet-5 in 1998. Work with NCR produced ATMs that read amounts on cheques and, from June 1996, back-office cheque readers that by 2001 were estimated to read 20 million checks a day, about 10 percent of all US checks.

mexico-hoy-no-circula-1989.summary: On 20 November 1989, facing winter ozone and lead levels among the worst recorded in any city, Mexico City's government made a voluntary scheme compulsory: every private car stays off roads one weekday a week according to last digit of its plate, enforced by coloured stickers. Studies of hourly monitoring data found no lasting improvement in air quality: households bought additional, often older and dirtier, vehicles to keep driving, total gasoline sales and driving rose, and weekend and off-hour traffic increased. Later versions added emissions testing exemptions and Saturday restrictions, and other cities from Bogotá to São Paulo and Beijing copied plate-based rationing. The programme became a standard case in environmental economics of how restrictions shift behaviour rather than cut emissions.

sources.title: Davis, Lucas W., 'The Effect of Driving Restrictions on Air Quality in Mexico City', Journal of Political Economy 116, no. 1 (2008)
sources.author: Davis, Lucas W.
sources.confirms: No evidence of improved air quality; increase in vehicles, shift toward high-emission cars.

Programme start dates vary slightly across sources; 20 November 1989 is widely cited. Plates ending in 5 and 6 rested Monday, 7 and 8 Tuesday, 3 and 4 Wednesday, 1 and 2 Thursday, 9 and 0 Friday. Owners of newer cars meeting emission tests gained exemption from 1997, which shifted fleet composition. Mexico City's ozone improved in later years, attributed more to unleaded fuel, catalytic converters and closure of 18 de Marzo refinery in 1991 than to driving bans.

q-learning-1989.summary: In 1989 Watkins's Q-learning let an agent learn the value of actions from delayed rewards, without requiring a model of its environment. “Q” names its central function, which estimates each action’s expected reward, its quality. Given enough exploration it finds an optimal policy for any finite Markov decision process; Watkins and Peter Dayan proved its convergence in 1992. DeepMind’s deep Q-learning later played Atari games at expert human levels.

sources.title: Q-learning
Watkins, Christopher J. C. H., and Peter Dayan, 'Q-learning', Machine Learning 8 (1992), pp. 279-292
sources.author: Watkins, Christopher J. C. H.; Dayan, Peter
sources.confirms: Q-learning (Watkins, 1989) lets agents learn to act optimally in Markovian domains by improving estimates of action values; the paper proves its convergence.

sources.title: Watkins, Christopher J. C. H., 'Learning from Delayed Rewards', PhD thesis, King's College, University of Cambridge, 1989
sources.author: Watkins, Christopher J. C. H.
sources.confirms: Watkins's 1989 doctoral thesis, the primary document introducing Q-learning as a method for learning action values from delayed rewards.

q-learning-1989.detail: Agents try actions and update their estimates from rewards received. In a grid maze, for instance, an agent learning to reach an exit worth 10 points comes to value turning right over left at some junction if right reaches that exit sooner. Q-learning handles stochastic transitions and rewards without adaptation, and its optimality holds given infinite exploration time and a partly random policy. Stevo Bozinovski’s Crossbar Adaptive Array had solved the same problem under the name “delayed reinforcement learning” in 1981. In 2014 Google DeepMind patented “deep Q-learning,” whose deep convolutional network played Atari 2600 games at expert human levels. Double DQN followed in 2015 to correct Q-learning’s tendency to overestimate action values in noisy environments.

singapore-tradenet-1989.summary: Singapore's Trade Development Board launches TradeNet on 1 January 1989, an EDI system built with Singapore Network Services that lets traders submit one electronic declaration routed to customs and about twenty agencies. Approvals that took two to four days and many paper forms return in minutes, and by 1991 nearly all declarations pass through it. Studies by Boon Siong Neo and by Teo, Tan and Wei analyse how agency process redesign, not software alone, produced gains in port throughput and reduced costs. UNECE and World Customs Organization later cite TradeNet as a model for single-window systems adopted across ASEAN and beyond.

universal-approximation-1989.summary: In 1989 George Cybenko proved that a neural network with one hidden layer can approximate any continuous function to any desired accuracy, given a non-polynomial activation function and enough neurons in that layer. He introduced the concept of discriminatory functions as a broader framework for sigmoid-type activation functions. These are existence theorems: they give no method for finding a network’s parameters or saying how large it must be.

sources.title: Universal approximation theorem
Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function
sources.author: Cybenko, George
sources.venue: Mathematics of Control, Signals and Systems 2, 303-314
sources.confirms: Proves that finite sums of sigmoidal functions, a single hidden layer network, can approximate any continuous function on the unit cube.

sources.title: Hornik, Kurt, Stinchcombe, Maxwell and White, Halbert, 'Multilayer feedforward networks are universal approximators', Neural Networks 2, no. 5 (1989) 359-366
sources.author: Kurt Hornik, Maxwell Stinchcombe and Halbert White
sources.confirms: In the same year as Cybenko, Hornik, Stinchcombe and White independently proved that standard multilayer feedforward networks with one hidden layer can approximate any measurable function to any desired accuracy.
sources.qualifies: The non-polynomial activation condition in the record comes from later work (Leshno et al. 1993), not Cybenko's sigmoidal proof.

universal-approximation-1989.detail: Cybenko had proved the result for sigmoidal networks in March 1988. Ken-ichi Funahashi’s May 1988 ATR report reinterpreted the Kolmogorov–Arnold–Sprecher theorem for neural networks and showed that Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams’s four-layer network with sigmoid hidden units could approximate arbitrary continuous mappings. His May 1989 proof, starting from Irie and Miyake’s integral representation, covered networks with one hidden layer and extended by induction to any number of layers. Hornik, Stinchcombe and White extended it in 1989 to unbounded, non-monotonic, discontinuous and measurable activation functions with a proof from the Stone–Weierstrass theorem. Later versions showed universality can also be reached by fixing width and adding depth, and these theorems are cited as mathematical justification for applying neural networks to complex non-linear relationships.

unsw-perc-solar-cell-1989.summary: At University of New South Wales, Martin Green, Andrew Blakers, Aihua Wang, Jianhua Zhao and Adele Milne described a passivated emitter and rear cell (PERC) in Applied Physics Letters in September 1989, with independently confirmed efficiency of 22.8 percent, highest yet for silicon. PERC added a thin oxide passivation layer on rear surface with small point contacts, cutting electron recombination and reflecting light back through wafer. Group had already set records with passivated emitter cells in 1980s. PERC stayed a laboratory design for two decades until manufacturers in China adopted it around 2012; by 2020 PERC cells made up more than 80 percent of global solar module production.

Dullweber and Schmidt review industrial PERC lines reaching 22 percent. Zhengrong Shi, a Green student, founded Suntech in 2001, carrying UNSW know-how to China. Green's group later pushed silicon to 25 percent and now works on tandem cells. UNSW photovoltaics also trained many engineers in China's solar industry.

vietnam-resolution-10-rice-exports-1989.summary: Politburo Resolution 10 of April 1988 dissolves collective farming in practice: households receive land-use rights for 10 to 15 years, keep output after taxes and sell at market prices, while 1989 reforms free input and rice markets and devalue currency. Pingali and Vo-Tong Xuan show that decollectivisation, applied to irrigated Mekong and Red River deltas already using modern varieties, lifted paddy output by about 10 percent in a single season. Vietnam, which imported rice in 1987 and 1988, exports 1.4 million tonnes in 1989 and ranks third among exporters. Rural incomes and later coffee and aquaculture exports followed this agricultural turn of Doi Moi.

www-proposal-1989.summary: In 1989 Tim Berners-Lee proposed linking documents on any computer with hypertext: the Web. CERN’s physicists needed to store and find documents across incompatible computers, so he linked documents by hypertext, text carrying links that jump to other documents, each reachable through its own address over shared rules. By late 1990 he had working browser and server software; CERN released it to other institutions in January 1991, to the whole Internet on 23 August 1991, and royalty-free on 30 April 1993.

sources.title: World Wide Web - Wikipedia
Information Management: A Proposal
sources.author: Berners-Lee, Tim
sources.confirms: The original March 1989 proposal for a hypertext system linking documents across CERN's incompatible computers.

sources.title: The World-Wide Web
sources.author: Berners-Lee, Tim; Cailliau, Robert; Luotonen, Ari; Nielsen, Henrik Frystyk; Secret, Arthur
sources.confirms: Peer-reviewed account of the Web's design and its release from CERN in 1991.

www-proposal-1989.detail:
His March 1989 proposal was unnamed; it aimed at managing information in a large, constantly changing organisation and distributing it to collaborators outside CERN. It drew on his 1980 ENQUIRE program and Ted Nelson’s 1965 hypertext model. Berners-Lee dismissed tree structures such as CERNDOC and Unix’s filesystem and keyword tagging as in VAX/NOTES; unlike Apple’s HyperCard, his system was meant from its outset to link multiple databases on independent machines. By late 1990 he had written his WorldWideWeb browser-editor, the first HTTP server, and first versions of HTTP, URL syntax and HTML.

Within two years of public release there were 50 websites. After NCSA’s Mosaic browser arrived later in 1993, thousands of websites appeared in under a year; Marc Andreessen and Jim Clark founded Netscape in 1994. Berners-Lee founded the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) to steward Web standards.

argentina-no-till-soy-1990.summary: From about 1988 farmers in Argentina's Pampas abandoned ploughing for siembra directa, sowing through crop residue with locally built seeders. AAPRESID, a farmers' association founded in 1989 in Rosario, and INTA extension agronomists spread this technique as soil erosion, falling fertility and tillage costs pressed on wheat and maize growers. Glyphosate-tolerant soybeans approved in 1996 fitted this system and soy area grew from about 5 to 20 million hectares by 2010. Peiretti and Dumanski record no-till covering around 27 million hectares, roughly 90 percent of grain area, by 2012, a share unmatched by any other country. Argentine seeder makers such as Agrometal and Crucianelli exported machines across South America and to Russia and Africa.

argentina-no-till-soy-1990.detail: Brazil's Paraná state began no-till in 1972 with Herbert Bartz and later developed it for smallholders, as de Freitas and Landers describe. Benefits included reduced erosion and fuel use and higher water retention; critics point to herbicide dependence, glyphosate-resistant weeds and soybean monoculture displacing cattle and forest in Chaco woodlands.

ataturk-dam-euphrates-impounded-1990.summary: On 13 January 1990 Turkey's State Hydraulic Works closes Atatürk Dam and cuts Euphrates flow to Syria and Iraq for a month to begin filling a reservoir of 48 cubic kilometres, after giving notice and releasing extra water in advance. Dam, a 169 metre rock-fill structure near Şanlıurfa, is centrepiece of Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP), a 22-dam scheme to irrigate 1.8 million hectares and generate 27 billion kilowatt hours a year. Turbines start in 1992 and twin 26 kilometre Şanlıurfa tunnels carry water to Harran plain from 1995. Cotton output in region soars; so do salinisation and waterlogging on poorly drained soils, while downstream states protest cuts. GAP becomes a reference case in water-conflict studies.

brazil-sus-unified-health-system-1990.summary: On 19 September 1990 President Collor signed Lei Orgânica da Saúde 8.080, giving legal form to Sistema Único de Saúde, which Brazil's 1988 constitution had declared a right of all and a state duty. Built by public health doctors and activists of Brazil's sanitarista movement during its return to democracy, SUS merged social-security hospitals, federal and state services into one tax-funded system, free at point of use, decentralised to more than 5,500 municipalities with community health councils. Its Family Health Strategy teams, started in 1994, reached about two thirds of Brazilians by 2015. A 2011 assessment credits SUS with falling infant mortality and expanded vaccination and antiretroviral treatment, and records chronic underfunding and a parallel private sector.

Reviewers in 2019 assessed thirty years of outcomes and risks from 2016's spending cap. SUS coordinated Brazil's COVID-19 vaccination in 2021, delivering over 400 million doses.

eff-founded-1990.summary: In July 1990 Mitch Kapor and John Perry Barlow founded the Electronic Frontier Foundation after Secret Service raids on hackers. Mitch Kapor, John Perry Barlow, and John Gilmore formed it with assistance from Steve Wozniak. Earlier that year Secret Service agents had seized Steve Jackson Games’ computers in Austin, and no existing civil liberties group understood its technology well enough to help. EFF announced it was representing Steve Jackson Games against the Secret Service, and a court held for the first time that electronic mail deserves at least as much protection as telephone calls.

sources.title: A History of Protecting Freedom Where Law and ...
EFF Is Turning 25 and We Want to Celebrate With You
EFF's 35th Anniversary
Electronic Frontier Foundation

eff-founded-1990.detail:
Secret Service agents were tracking copies of BellSouth’s E911 document, illegally copied from BellSouth’s computers, which described how emergency 911 systems worked. They searched Steve Jackson’s premises under warrant, took all electronic equipment and copies of an upcoming game book, later returned them and pressed no charges, having found no E911 copies. Kapor, former president of Lotus Development Corporation, Barlow, Wyoming cattle rancher and Grateful Dead lyricist, and Gilmore, early Sun Microsystems employee, had followed events on the WELL (Whole Earth ’Lectronic Link); EFF announced its Steve Jackson Games representation on its first day. EFF, San Francisco-based and nonprofit, formed in response to Operation Sundevil.

EFF’s second big case, Bernstein v. U.S. Dept. of Justice, challenged Washington’s position that Bernstein, then a mathematics PhD student at the University of California, needed an arms-dealer licence before posting his encryption program online; that court ruled for the first time that written software code is speech protected by the First Amendment.

hubble-space-telescope-1990.summary: In April 1990 the Hubble Space Telescope launched with a flawed mirror; once fixed in 1993 it pinned down our universe's age and expansion rate. Orbiting above Earth’s distorting atmosphere, its 2.4 m mirror was meant to give far sharper images than ground-based telescopes, but that mirror had been ground to the wrong shape, its outer edge too flat by about 2,200 nanometres, blurring every image. A servicing mission, STS-61, corrected Hubble’s optics to their intended quality in 1993 by installing corrective optics called COSTAR, and Hubble’s data cut uncertainty in the universe’s expansion rate from up to 50 percent to about 10 percent.

Okolski, Gabriel, 'A Brief History of the Hubble Space Telescope', NASA History (2008)
sources.author: Okolski, Gabriel
sources.confirms: The page says Hubble launched aboard Discovery on April 24, 1990, had a primary-mirror spherical aberration because the mirror edges were ground slightly too flat, and was repaired during the December 1993 STS-61 mission using COSTAR and a replacement Wide Field/Planetary Camera.
sources.qualifies: The source attributes the proof that the universe is expanding to Edwin P. Hubble, not to the repaired telescope.

sources.title: Allen, Lew et al., The Hubble Space Telescope Optical Systems Failure Report, NASA Technical Memorandum 103443 (Washington, DC: NASA, November 1990)
sources.author: Lew Allen et al. (HST Optical Systems Board of Investigation)
sources.confirms: The board found the primary mirror, made by Perkin-Elmer, had been ground to the wrong shape (0.4-wave rms wavefront error at 632.8 nm) because a lens in the reflective null corrector used as a template was mis-spaced.
sources.qualifies: States the error as wavefront error, not as an edge height.

hubble-space-telescope-1990.verification_note: Launch in April 1990, a mis-shaped primary mirror and 1993's STS-61 repair are confirmed; Allen's board measured that mirror error as 0.4 wave rms wavefront at 632.8 nm and traced it to a mis-spaced lens in a reflective null corrector, a wavefront figure sources do not convert to an edge error of about 2,200 nanometres. Edwin P. Hubble established cosmic expansion in 1929, and this telescope named for him narrowed its rate's uncertainty to about 10 percent.
hubble-space-telescope-1990.detail:
That flaw, spherical aberration, was traced by Lew Allen’s investigation to Perkin-Elmer’s null corrector, used to test its mirror during grinding, which had one lens 1.3 mm out of position. Charles Pellerin, NASA’s astrophysics director, reprioritised his division’s budget to allocate $60 million for repair; other component failures pushed repair cost to $500 million, not counting its shuttle flight. Hubble is the only telescope designed to be maintained in space by astronauts, and five shuttle missions between 1993 and May 2009 repaired or replaced systems including all five main instruments.

Hubble measurements of Cepheid variable stars in the Virgo Cluster and other galaxy clusters fixed the Hubble constant to within 10 percent. Two teams observing distant supernovae with ground-based telescopes and Hubble found cosmic expansion accelerating rather than slowing, work later recognised with Nobel Prizes and attributed to an unknown cause named dark energy. Named for Edwin Hubble, it is among NASA’s Great Observatories and is run by the Space Telescope Science Institute and Goddard Space Flight Center.

human-genome-project-launch-1990.summary: In 1990 America launched a $3 billion project to read all 3 billion letters of human DNA, a 15-year plan. A working draft was announced on 26 June 2000 and the essentially complete sequence on 14 April 2003, two years early, covering about 92 percent of that genome for roughly $2.7 billion.
